lxc_2172df0d2a2632d2.text: Borough Market has more than 100 stalls and shops in London.

lxc_feb7d02c93648983.text: They are spread across Three Crown Square, Green Market and Borough Market Kitchen.

lxc_c7d4ae45880ab776.text: Visitors can buy British seafood, regional cheese and cured meat, or stop for Middle Eastern meze, falafel or shawarma.

lxc_ec135b960c73cb5f.text: Cakes, pastries and bao buns add quick sweet and savoury choices.

lxc_ae75f1a2af86f08e.text: The market works well for two different plans: shopping for ingredients to take home or choosing lunch and eating it nearby.

lxc_59d2a240f6c2dcc6.text: Moving through its three areas shows how many kinds of food one market can bring together.

lxc_dbd0fd6ad83eb589.text: Marché des Enfants Rouges is a small covered market in Paris.

lxc_8bd17285f3220a6a.text: Founded in 1615, it is the city's oldest covered food market.

lxc_df5348541041fcdb.text: Fresh produce and farm cheese share the space with counters serving ready-to-eat food.

lxc_96a7746f38ff2e4c.text: A visitor might see chicken skewers, vegetable couscous or a Breton buckwheat galette.

lxc_df7493f8c4095b51.text: Other choices include oysters and fresh fruit juice.

lxc_d2c0158fdd732bd5.text: The prepared food comes from several food cultures, so a short walk can reveal very different flavours.

lxc_f16117d85bb747f8.text: It is an easy place to choose a simple lunch while enjoying the close, historic market atmosphere.

lxc_c48fb55ddd0df536.text: Visit three famous European food markets in Barcelona, Paris and London.

lxc_5371b5ead89f1ead.text: Learn what you can find there, then practise the English you need to choose food, check ingredients, pay and tip.

lxc_b997e2de9ed9ae68.text: La Boqueria sits on La Rambla in Barcelona.

lxc_a10d962331c68410.text: It has served the city as a market since 1836, and today more than 200 traders work there.

lxc_3fba4996561112ae.text: Bright fruit and vegetable stalls stand beside sellers of olives and preserved foods.

lxc_ef1e69552e54d4bc.text: Visitors can also find nuts and pulses, poultry and eggs, meat, fish and seafood.

lxc_3089e6ee3ca5021a.text: Grocery stalls provide everyday ingredients, while small bars offer a place to stop and eat.

lxc_ee4137afa7531959.text: This mix makes La Boqueria more than a sightseeing stop: it is a working food market where visitors can compare fresh produce, specialist foods and ready-to-eat dishes.

lxc_9bc67a656b37a6ea.text: At a simple market stall or self-service counter, people normally pay the displayed price unless the seller says otherwise.

lxc_810c6ef15fea1a5e.text: In Spain, a tip is optional, and some people simply round up the bill.

lxc_39b01d3997bf38b8.text: In France, restaurant prices normally include service, so extra money is optional.
